summary.text: A 19-year-old immunocompetent male from the countryside of Aleppo, Syria, presented with generalized infiltrating papules, plaques and nodules, leonine facial appearance, eyebrow alopecia and bilateral auricular edema since 2022. The disease began as a single facial nodule.
Cryotherapy with liquid nitrogen, intralesional antimonial injections and systemic antimonial therapy did not control the lesions, and lepromatous leprosy was suspected.

Work-up showed mild anemia, elevated C-reactive protein, increased IgG and IgM, negative HIV and tuberculin tests, and normal ultrasound of the liver, gallbladder, spleen, kidneys and peritoneum. Wade staining was unavailable and PCR was not performed.
Skin biopsy histopathology showed Donovan bodies with negative Ziehl-Neelsen staining and no characteristic leprosy features, establishing diffuse cutaneous leishmaniasis and excluding leprosy.
Systemic amphotericin B was started as second-line treatment; initial clinical improvement was seen 1 week after treatment, but the response then plateaued with no further progress.
